idiom_name: class/function template storing a callable renderer (lambda or std::function)
implementation_notes: The owner is a class or function template that stores a callable and invokes it with the current state; std::function - documented as a general-purpose polymorphic function wrapper that can store, copy and invoke any CopyConstructible callable target - keeps the owner non-generic and replaceable at runtime, while a template parameter keeps the call site inlineable and allocation-free. Either way the caller's lambda is the only place markup is assembled and the owner keeps the state. Reach for type erasure when the callable must be stored in a non-template class or swapped later; use the template parameter in headers that can afford to be generic. The Qt variant replaces both with QStyledItemDelegate when the rendering already lives inside a model/view widget.
pitfalls: A std::function member is empty until assigned and invoking an empty std::function throws std::bad_function_call, so the owner must require a callable at construction.
A lambda stored in a long-lived owner that captures by reference dangles as soon as the referenced object dies; capture by value or keep ownership explicit.
Type erasure through std::function costs an allocation for large captures and blocks inlining; in hot paths prefer the template parameter.

variants.name: Qt model/view item delegate
variants.idiom_name: QStyledItemDelegate subclass painting each item for the view
variants.implementation_notes: Qt's model/view framework already implements the split: the view asks a delegate to paint every item, so the caller-supplied delegate - not the framework - decides the visual for each piece of model state. The documentation describes QStyledItemDelegate as the default delegate for all item views and directs customizations to subclassing it and reimplementing paint() and sizeHint(), with paint() called individually for each item. Choose it when the rendering lives in a Qt item view and a delegate can own the painting; keep the plain callable component when the output is not item-shaped.
pitfalls: The delegate paints into a shared painter; forgetting to save/restore QPainter state leaks pen and font changes into neighbouring items - the docs require returning the painter to its supplied state.
Editors also fall to the delegate (createEditor/setModelData), so a render-only customization still has to keep the default editing path working.
